subject: Pilot close conditions — sprint exit blueprint and acceptance tests
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amina Patel <amina.patel@medsyshealth.com>, MedSys Procurement <procure@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot close conditions — sprint exit blueprint and acceptance tests

Amina / procurement team —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I drafted a compact sprint-based MAP that defines the minimum pass/fail conditions we need to agree on to move from pilot → committed contract. The attached MAP-sprint-blueprint-v1.xlsx is intentionally short — it focuses on 3 sprints (2 weeks each) and the absolute exit gates. High level, the acceptance buckets are:

- Functional correctness: example prompt sets (50 canonical flows) must meet a top-line quality threshold (F1/accuracy target depending on use case).
- Latency & reliability: P95 token-generation latency <= 220ms for 95% of requests during test windows; 99.9% uptime for the dedicated path.
- Data & security: audit log delivery and retention verified; SOC 2 or equivalent evidence provided.
- Cost: projected unit cost (tokens + infra) within agreed threshold (we show a target under $0.045 per 1k tokens for the pilot profile).
- Integration: API contract tests and end-to-end sample with your sample dataset (see test plan tab).

Exit gates (all required to pass final signoff):
1) QA: 50/50 random sample acceptance >= 85% (or pre-agreed metric) on the canonical flows.
2) Perf: All P95 measurements in the final 48h window meet the latency target.
3) Security: SOC 2 in-scope evidence + completed ISV questionnaire responses.
4) Procurement: SOW and commercial terms signed or DocuSign envelope issued.

What I need from you now:
- Confirmation that the four exit gates cover MedSys signoff needs (flag anything missing).
- Any hard constraints on audit log retention (e.g., 180 days vs 365 days).
- Procurement target date for signature (we tentatively have Oct 14 for internal review).

Next steps: If you confirm the exit gates, Ben will share a tight SOW and we can schedule the two test windows (week of Oct 20 and Oct 27).

Thanks —
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-sprint-blueprint-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 6 tabs: summary, tests, telemetry, roles, SOW notes, timeline)
From: Amina Patel <amina.patel@medsyshealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSys Procurement <procure@medsyshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot close conditions — sprint exit blueprint and acceptance tests

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful and much clearer than our internal notes. A couple quick clarifying items from our side:

1) Audit logs/retention: our policy requires immutable audit logs retained for 365 days, and a mechanism to export to our archival S3. Is that straightforward?
2) SOC 2: we have an internal checklist. If you can share SOC 2 Type II report or an equivalent attestation + contact for a security review, procurement will be comfortable.
3) Acceptance metric: the QA sample approach works — can you confirm whether the 85% is measured by us or by Redwood and whether there will be shared tooling/report to reproduce scoring?
4) Timeline: procurement wants final SOW and any redlines by Oct 12 so they can complete approvals by Oct 14. Can Redwood commit to that turnaround?

If we can get the SOC 2 evidence and confirm the log export, procurement will be OK slotting the signature review for Oct 14.

Best,
Amina

--
Amina Patel
Head of AI Integrations | MedSys Health
amina.patel@medsyshealth.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amina Patel <amina.patel@medsyshealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot close conditions — sprint exit blueprint and acceptance tests

Amina — quick answers and what we can deliver this week: 

- Audit logs: yes — we can push immutable audit exports to an S3 bucket you control. We'll include an automated daily export plus on-demand snapshot for the final validation window.
- SOC 2: I attached our SOC 2 summary and a redacted attestation; our security team can set up a brief call with your security reviewer if they'd like the full Type II review under an NDA.
- Scoring/tooling: Redwood will run the canonical scoring run and provide the full scoring report (reproducible scripts + datasets) in the shared Drive. You'll have read-only access, and we can provide a small test harness so your team can re-run locally if needed.

Marcus — I'm attaching a first-pass SOW (SOW-draft-MedSys-2026-10.pdf). I'm flagging the commercial milestones tied to the exit gates so procurement can see the link between test outcomes and invoicing.

Amina — can you confirm the procurement review owner (name/email) so I can share the DocuSign package when terms are final?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0266

Attachment: SOW-draft-MedSys-2026-10.pdf (draft, highlights financial milestones and trial window)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amina Patel <amina.patel@medsyshealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot close conditions — sprint exit blueprint and acceptance tests

Amina / team — quick internal confirmation from Redwood:

- We accept the 365-day audit retention requirement and will configure daily immutable exports to your S3 archive during the pilot validation windows.
- Security: Ben's attached attestation will be supplemented with a security reviewer call this week. We can provide the full Type II under NDA prior to final signoff.
- Scoring: Redwood will produce the reproducible scoring report and grant MedSys read-only Drive access; we'll include the test harness as promised.
- SOW & timing: Ben, please finalize the SOW with the commercial milestones linked to the exit gates. Once procurement confirms the review owner, we'll issue the DocuSign envelope.

Go / no-go review: set for Fri, Oct 22 at 10:00 AM PT (we'll use this meeting to review the final 48h test window and sign). If procurement still needs Oct 14 for internal sign-off, we can support that date — but the go/no-go requires the final telemetry window.

Amina — feel free to add any procurement inbox/contact and we'll route the DocuSign and the SOW immediately.

Laura

--
